solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A possibly essential cut by minister

indicators.note: a word that has been cut is shortened, so its final letter is trimmed away

parts.note: essential means vital
MIN is a standard abbreviation for minister

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a cut in pay or budget made by a government minister might be essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A looks like the article; it is the letter naming one example of the answer. Cut VITAL to VITA, then put MIN beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin A is one member of the class of vitamins, so the letter with 'possibly' works as a definition by example.

clue.text: V and X? Not G and RESPECT!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: 'not' tells the solver to leave out the letter that follows it from the word just built

parts.note: Generation X, so X can stand for a generation
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: It reads like a puzzled comment on Roman numerals and a demand for respect, as if G were being snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: V and X look like Roman numerals, but X stands for a generation, as in Generation X. Drop its G and put V in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration is deep reverence or high regard, a close synonym for respect shown to someone admired.

clue.text: When high, I often get my wires crossed

definitions.text: When high, I often get my wires crossed

parts.words: When high, I often get my wires crossed
parts.note: surface reading: someone intoxicated who gets confused and misunderstands things

parts.words: When high, I often get my wires crossed
parts.note: setter's reading: a circus performer high above the ring who literally crosses along wires

explanation.walkthrough: 'High' suggests being drunk or drugged and 'get my wires crossed' is the idiom for misunderstanding; read literally, the speaker is up high walking across wires.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer balancing on a taut cable high above the ground spends the act traversing wires, so the literal reading describes the job.

clue.text: Extremely small comic rocked shows

indicators.note: to show something is to display it, so the letters are on view inside the words before

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A comedian so tiny they rocked the audience, or a small comic who put on rocking shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'comic' into the start of 'rocked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Micro is used as an adjective for things of very tiny size or scale, as in microcomputer or micro business.

clue.text: Telltale sailor managed to upset men

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so in a down clue the letters are turned the other way

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
to run a business is to manage it
OR, other ranks, means the ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A sailor who tells tales managed to upset his shipmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telltale' looks like a sneak, but it is read as one who tells a tale. OR (other ranks) is the crossword stock for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'tell tale', the word describes a storyteller, which is exactly what a narrator does in a book or play.

clue.text: Small peninsula in big bit of Russia

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone locates a small peninsula somewhere in a large region of Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a location but only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast northern Asian region makes up most of Russian territory, stretching from the Urals to the Pacific.

clue.text: Obsessed fan drinking one Sol slurs

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside itself, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a stan is slang for an obsessive fan, from the Eminem song
I is the Roman numeral one
S is the tonic sol-fa abbreviation for sol (soh)

explanation.surface: An obsessive fan knocking back a Sol beer starts slurring words.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol looks like the Mexican lager, and 'slurs' like drunken speech; I goes inside STAN, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on someone's character is a blemish on reputation, so stains and slurs are synonyms as plural nouns.

clue.text: Is hob mean to mess around hipsters?

indicators.note: messing around with something throws it into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a kitchen hob is meant for trendy people to fool around with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hob' and 'mean' look like kitchen talk and meanness; all nine letters of the first three words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemians are unconventional, arty people living outside mainstream norms, much the same crowd now called hipsters.

clue.text: A teenage starlet cast for Broadway job

definitions.note: names the occupation, while the answer names the person who does it

indicators.note: to cast is to mould into a new shape, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young actress is chosen for a part in a Broadway show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'Broadway' point to theatre, but 'cast' reshuffles the fifteen letters and Broadway stands for America, where the term is used for the job the British call estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Real-estate agent is the American title for someone who sells houses and land, the job Britons call estate agent.

clue.text: Mirror son breaks in part of church

indicators.note: a burglar who breaks in gets inside, so one piece enters another

parts.note: to ape is to mirror or copy
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son smashes a mirror while inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mirror' looks like a noun for a looking glass but is the verb, meaning to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually housing the altar.

clue.text: Horse or badger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old or worn-out horse
second meaning: to pester someone repeatedly

explanation.walkthrough: Horse and badger look like two animals to choose between, but badger is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a noun for a tired old horse and as a verb for pestering someone with complaints.

clue.text: Range of trains a chap redesigned

indicators.note: something redesigned has been put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man has redesigned a whole product range of model trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a product line, but it is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carpathians are a long mountain chain arcing through central and eastern Europe, from Slovakia to Romania.

clue.text: For one, seven men abort urinal trips

indicators.note: whatever trips stumbles and falls in a heap, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seven men, for one reason or another, call off their trips to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seven men' reads as a group, but seven belongs with 'For one' as an example; the fodder begins at 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number and so can be written as a ratio of integers, making it one example of that class.

clue.text: Rational grounds to get fit

parts.note: grounds for doing something are the reason
fit to do something means able to do it

explanation.surface: Someone offers sensible reasons for getting into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests land and 'fit' healthy, but they mean reason and capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe thinking or behaviour that is sensible, logical and in accordance with sound judgement.

clue.text: Make fast cash around hardware store

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to moor a boat is to make it fast
loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: A tip for making quick money: flog things around a hardware shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast cash' reads as earning quickly, but 'make fast' means tie up, a nautical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolroom is a room where tools and equipment are kept, so it stores hardware, loosely a hardware store.

clue.text: Just hit rogues in need of correction

indicators.note: something needing correction is currently wrong, so these letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vigilante's line: simply beat up villains who need to be set straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'simply', but it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means morally right and fair, which is what righteous describes.

clue.text: Deliver dog-eared veg up north

indicators.note: to deliver a speech is to say it out loud, so the sound of a word is what counts

parts.note: dog-eared pages look worn and shabby

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to deliver some worn-looking vegetables to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' suggests a courier, but it means utter. 'Up north' marks a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattie is the Scots and northern English word for a potato, the staple vegetable.

clue.text: What's left over after taking a note?

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so a letter comes out of the word

parts.note: the remainder is what is left over
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what remains once you have jotted something down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a riddle about leftovers; the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A note left for yourself or someone else to prompt memory of a task is exactly a reminder.

clue.text: Nervy individual with 500K note

parts.note: a single individual is one
D is the Roman numeral for 500
K and G both mean a thousand, G for a grand
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A person is anxious about carrying a banknote worth half a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 500K reads as one sum of money but splits into 500 and K; K and G are both slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being tense and jumpy, the state of someone nervy.

clue.text: Places surfers go in mesh spectacles, I'm told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a web is a mesh and sights are spectacles

explanation.surface: Surfers visit spots with netted sights, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Surfers sound like wave riders, but these are internet surfers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who browse online are said to surf the net, and the pages they visit are online destinations.

clue.text: Gallons consumed by upset mathematician to get fix again

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue the letters are turned upside down
something consumed ends up inside what consumes it

parts.note: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: A distraught mathematician downs gallons to get another fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' suggests a drug hit for a drinker, but it is the verb meaning mend.
explanation.definitionFit: To reglue something is to stick it back together with adhesive, repairing or fixing it a second time.

clue.text: Dreams of properties on the Costa del Sol?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for unrealistic hopes or daydreams

definitions.text: properties on the Costa del Sol?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsically literal: fortified buildings on Spain's southern coast

explanation.walkthrough: The Costa del Sol is Spain's sunny southern coastline, popular with British holiday-home buyers; the question mark flags the playful literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The old idiom means fanciful plans or daydreams unlikely to come true, like air castles.

clue.text: Flight path?

parts.note: surface reading: the route an aircraft follows through the sky
setter's reading: the way up formed by a flight of stairs

explanation.walkthrough: A flight is also a set of stairs, so the path of such a flight is made of treads you climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is called a flight, and its individual treads provide the route you walk up it.

clue.text: Army chaplain saves a large beast

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safely held, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: CF is Chaplain to the Forces
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A military padre rescues a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' looks like it describes the beast, but it gives L; CF, Chaplain to the Forces, is the British army title.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is a young cow, and beast is a general word for any farm animal or creature.

clue.text: Give thanks for a Conservative awareness

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
awareness of something is knowledge of it

explanation.surface: Someone expresses gratitude for a Tory politician's consciousness of an issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge a gift or help is to express gratitude publicly, as in acknowledgements at the front of a book.

clue.text: King, perhaps English, rebuffed decline

indicators.note: a rebuff pushes something back, so the letters go the opposite direction

parts.note: B.B. King was the American blues guitarist
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A monarch, possibly English, snubbed and refused an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' suggests a monarch, but it is a surname, and 'perhaps' asks for a first name: BB King.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede or dwindle, like a falling tide, so it is a synonym for decline as a verb.

clue.text: Expect Spooner's irritated with charge

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places here

parts.note: irritated skin is sore
a fee is a charge
swapping the first sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: Anticipate that the Reverend will be annoyed about being billed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces; swap their opening S and F sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to predict or anticipate it before it happens, the verb sense of expect.

clue.text: Prize plant dry, getting hose finally

parts.note: a rose is a plant
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the word is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prizewinning plant has dried out and finally gets watered with the hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like parched soil but means teetotal; TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded to winners at shows, so it is a prize given for first place.
